context.analysis:
## Overview
[The Insurance Claims Modernization platform gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a modern Azure-hosted web application. It enables incremental claim-type migration while the legacy system maintains the system of record.]

## Key Elements
* End Customers & Brokers
* Claims Adjusters
* Insurance Claims Modernization Platform (Azure App Service, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL)
* Legacy Mainframe (z/OS, DB2, CICS)
* Corporate Active Directory (Microsoft Entra ID / AD)
* Notification Service (SendGrid / Azure Communication Services)
* Payment Gateway (Regional Banking API)

## Relationships
* End Customers & Brokers -> Modern Platform (HTTPS)
* Claims Adjusters -> Modern Platform (HTTPS)
* Modern Platform <-> Legacy Mainframe (Asynchronous messaging / ETL via secure gateway with mTLS)
* Modern Platform -> Corporate Active Directory (OIDC/SAML)
* Modern Platform -> Notification Service (HTTPS)
* Modern Platform -> Payment Gateway (REST/JSON over mTLS with payload signatures)

## Technology Stack
* Azure App Service & Kubernetes: Cloud hosting for scalable containerized modern microservices
* PostgreSQL: Modern relational database for migrated claim types
* Microsoft Entra ID (Active Directory): Centralized IAM for SSO and RBAC
* Azure Key Vault: Secure management of secrets, API keys, and certificates
* OpenTelemetry: Distributed tracing across Azure and on-prem mainframe

## Rationale
[A hybrid architecture with an Anti-Corruption Layer decouples the modern Azure platform from the fragile legacy mainframe, ensuring strict data consistency and fast UI performance. This isolates expensive mainframe change cycles while enabling incremental claim migration and rapid rollbacks.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
- Hybrid modernization platform replacing an on-premises mainframe claims system gradually over three years.
- Enables online customer submissions, low-latency adjuster workflows, and secure claim-type migration.

## Key Elements
- End Customers & Brokers (Users)
- Claims Adjusters (Users)
- Legacy Mainframe (External System / System of Record)
- Corporate Active Directory (External System)
- API Gateway (Azure API Management / NGINX)
- Customer Portal (React / Node.js)
- Adjuster Workspace including Operations Dashboard (React / .NET Core API)
- Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer (.NET Core / MassTransit)
- Claim Read Model Database (Azure Cosmos DB)
- Configuration & Feature Store (Azure App Configuration / Redis)

## Relationships
- Customer Portal to API Gateway via HTTPS/REST
- Adjuster Workspace to API Gateway via HTTPS/REST
- API Gateway to Corporate Active Directory via OIDC/OAuth2 for SSO
- API Gateway to Microservices via Internal HTTPS/gRPC with OpenTelemetry
- Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer to Legacy Mainframe via MQ/Enterprise Service Bus over mTLS
- Adjuster Workspace to Claim Read Model Database via TCP/NoSQL

## Technology Stack
- Hybrid Cloud (Azure West Europe + On-Premises Mainframe) to balance legacy retention and modern scalability
- .NET Core and React for modern, maintainable microservices and UI components
- Azure Cosmos DB for low-latency read models supporting <2s UI requirements
- Azure API Management for dynamic routing, rate-limiting, and SSO validation
- Azure App Configuration for managing feature flags and one-day claim-type fallbacks
- Terraform/Bicep and GitOps (ArgoCD/Flux) for infrastructure automation

## Rationale
- Decouples legacy dependencies through an Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer to ensure zero lost claims and support gradual migration.
- Employs a CQRS pattern with Azure Cosmos DB to guarantee sub-2-second adjuster screens despite high mainframe latency.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is an Insurance Claims Modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a modern Azure-based cloud architecture. It ensures seamless hybrid operations for customer claim submissions and adjuster workflows while maintaining strict consistency and security.]

## Key Elements
- End Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- API Gateway (Azure API Management / NGINX)
- Customer Portal (React / Node.js)
- Adjuster Workspace (React / .NET Core API)
- Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer (.NET Core / MassTransit)
- Configuration & Feature Store (Azure App Configuration / Redis)
- Corporate Active Directory
- Azure Key Vault
- Legacy Mainframe

## Relationships
- End Customers & Brokers -> API Gateway: Accesses portal and submits claims [HTTPS/REST]
- Claims Adjusters -> API Gateway: Accesses adjuster workspace and processes claims [HTTPS/REST]
- API Gateway -> Corporate Active Directory: Validates SSO and authentication [OIDC/OAuth2]
- API Gateway -> Configuration & Feature Store: Fetches active routing rules [Internal HTTPS/REST, cached locally]
- API Gateway -> Azure Key Vault: Retrieves certificates and OAuth secrets [Azure Managed Identity / HTTPS]
- API Gateway -> Integration Layer: Forwards traffic with injected W3C trace context [mTLS / gRPC]

## Technology Stack
- Azure API Management: Provides dynamic path-based routing, WAF integration, and rate limiting
- Azure App Configuration & Redis: Stores feature flags and cached routing rules for rapid claim rollbacks
- .NET Core & MassTransit: Powers backend APIs and the Integration/Anti-Corruption Layer
- Azure Key Vault: Manages secrets and certificates securely using Managed Identities

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture isolates the expensive legacy mainframe behind an Anti-Corruption Layer while using dynamic API Gateway routing to migrate claim types incrementally. It satisfies non-functional requirements for low latency, secure SSO integration, zero data loss, and rapid one-day rollbacks.]

Customer Portal.analysis:
## Overview
[A hybrid modernization platform that gradually replaces a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system with a cloud-native Azure architecture while maintaining business continuity. The system processes online claims via a secure web portal while preserving legacy batch processing constraints.]

## Key Elements
* Customer Portal Container (React / Node.js)
* Claims SPA Component (React, TypeScript)
* Claim Validation & Mapping Component (Node.js, Zod)
* BFF Routing & Session Component (Node.js, Express)
* API Gateway (Azure API Management / NGINX)
* Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer (.NET Core / MassTransit)
* Legacy Mainframe System (COBOL/DB2)
* Corporate Active Directory / Azure AD

## Relationships
* Claims SPA -> Claim Validation & Mapping: Validates payloads locally [In-process]
* Claim Validation & Mapping -> BFF Routing & Session: Passes validated claim data [In-process]
* BFF Routing & Session -> API Gateway: Proxies authenticated requests [HTTPS / REST]
* API Gateway -> Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer: Routes domain requests [Internal HTTPS]
* Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer -> Legacy Mainframe: Synchronizes data [MQ / DB2 Connect]

## Technology Stack
* React & TypeScript: Frontend user interface for customer and broker claim submissions
* Node.js & Express: Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) handling sessions and API aggregation
* Zod: Server-side schema validation for input sanitization
* Azure Container Apps: Stateless containerized deployment target for the portal tier
* Azure Active Directory: Single sign-on authentication and RBAC via Azure Managed Identity
* OpenTelemetry & Azure Monitor: Distributed tracing and observability for hybrid latency tracking

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture isolates complex legacy mainframe dependencies behind an anti-corruption layer while delivering a modern, responsive web experience. It minimizes risk by migrating claim types incrementally, keeping migration downtime low and ensuring seamless compliance with security and latency constraints.]

Adjuster Workspace.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a cloud-native platform. It maintains dual-processing capabilities to ensure zero claim loss while migrating claim types sequentially.

## Key Elements
- End Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2)
- Azure API Management / NGINX (API Gateway)
- Customer Portal (React / Node.js)
- Adjuster Workspace (React / .NET Core API)
- Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer (.NET Core / MassTransit)
- Claim Read Model Database (Azure Cosmos DB)
- Corporate Active Directory (Azure AD / Entra ID)

## Relationships
- Customer Portal -> API Gateway: Submits claims [HTTPS/REST]
- Adjuster Workspace -> API Gateway: Routes adjuster traffic [Internal HTTPS]
- Adjuster Workspace -> Claim Read Model Database: Reads claim data [TCP / Cosmos DB Direct Mode]
- Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer -> Legacy Mainframe: Syncs data and routes commands [AMQP / MQ]
- Workspace API Backend -> Corporate Active Directory: Validates Single Sign-On [OIDC / OAuth2 / TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- React & TypeScript: Enables rapid UI state toggling and a platform fallback status banner for R-06.
- .NET Core Web API: Provides enterprise patterns and robust backend orchestration.
- Azure Cosmos DB: Delivers low-latency NoSQL reads to guarantee sub-2s screen loads (R-05).
- MassTransit & RabbitMQ: Manages asynchronous messaging and circuit breakers through the Anti-Corruption Layer.
- Azure Container Apps & Docker: Containerizes independent artifacts for reliable hybrid deployments.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture decouples modern user experiences from the rigid mainframe, meeting strict performance and fallback requirements. It mitigates team cloud-incurred risks using managed Azure services while preserving system of record consistency.

Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer.analysis:
## Overview
The system modernizes a regional insurer's 30-year-old mainframe by introducing a cloud-based platform using a strangler fig migration strategy. It enables online claims submission and adjuster workflows while keeping the mainframe as the system of record.

## Key Elements
- Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer (.NET Core / MassTransit)
- Translation Engine (.NET Core / FluentValidation)
- Outbox Processor (MassTransit / Entity Framework Core / Azure SQL Serverless)
- Async Sync Worker (MassTransit / Polly)
- Routing & Feature Router (Azure App Configuration)
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2)
- Azure API Management

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer [Internal HTTPS/gRPC]
- Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer -> Legacy Mainframe [IBM MQ over mTLS]
- Outbox Processor -> Azure SQL Serverless [ADO.NET / EF Core]
- Routing & Feature Router -> Azure App Configuration [REST / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- .NET Core: Selected for building high-performance, maintainable microservices with strong enterprise support.
- MassTransit: Chosen to implement reliable messaging patterns and handle asynchronous workflows.
- Azure SQL Serverless: Provides ACID guarantees for the Transactional Outbox pattern to prevent lost claims.
- IBM MQ: Ensures secure, enterprise-grade messaging protocol with the on-premise mainframe.
- Azure App Configuration: Manages dynamic feature flags for gradual claim-type migration and rollbacks.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe changes through an anti-corruption layer while ensuring sub-second UI performance. It guarantees transactional consistency and enables a risk-free, one-by-one claim migration path with rapid rollback capabilities.

Claim Read Model Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL mainframe with a cloud-native Azure platform. It modernizes customer claim submissions and adjuster workflows while maintaining seamless hybrid coexistence with the legacy system of record.

## Key Elements
- **Claim Read Model Database:** Azure Cosmos DB container storing denormalized low-latency views.
- **Claim Document Store:** Cosmos DB Core/SQL API component for JSON claim models.
- **Change Feed Processor:** Asynchronous event synchronization component.
- **Schema Version Router:** Lightweight routing component for backward compatibility.
- **Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer:** .NET Core / MassTransit service bridging mainframe and cloud.
- **Adjuster Workspace:** React / .NET Core web application for claims processing.

## Relationships
- Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer -> Claim Document Store: Writes projected claim models [TCP/HTTPS]
- Change Feed Processor -> Claim Document Store: Manages state synchronization [Cosmos DB SDK]
- Adjuster Workspace -> Schema Version Router: Requests claim read models [HTTPS/REST]
- Schema Version Router -> Claim Document Store: Retrieves versioned documents [TCP/Cosmos DB SDK]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Cosmos DB: Multi-model NoSQL database ensuring sub-2-second UI responses despite mainframe latency.
- .NET Core & MassTransit: Integration framework for reliable event-driven data synchronization.
- Terraform: Infrastructure-as-Code tool for deploying database and security components to mitigate low cloud experience.
- Microsoft Entra ID: Identity provider enforcing RBAC and JWT validation for Active Directory SSO.

## Rationale
This architecture uses a hybrid event-driven Cosmos DB read model to bypass mainframe latency constraints while ensuring zero data loss. It empowers an inexperienced cloud team through serverless scaling, automated IaC, and robust version routing.

Configuration & Feature Store.analysis:
## Overview
This system modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurer mainframe claims platform by migrating claim types incrementally to Azure while maintaining business continuity. The architecture uses a hybrid cloud approach to safely bridge legacy infrastructure with modern cloud services over a 3-year migration window.

## Key Elements
- End Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- API Gateway (Azure API Management / NGINX)
- Customer Portal (React / Node.js)
- Adjuster Workspace (React / .NET Core API)
- Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer (.NET Core / MassTransit)
- Configuration & Feature Store (Azure App Configuration)
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2)
- Corporate Active Directory

## Relationships
- Customers & Brokers to Customer Portal via HTTPS/TLS 1.3
- Adjusters to Adjuster Workspace via HTTPS/TLS 1.3
- Services to Configuration & Feature Store via HTTPS with Azure Managed Identities
- Integration & Anti-Corruption Layer to Legacy Mainframe via IBM MQ / TCP
- Users to Corporate Active Directory via OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 (SSO)

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud Platform:** Microsoft Azure (West Europe region) for minimal operational overhead
- **Compute & Integration:** .NET Core and MassTransit for reliable message handling
- **Frontend:** React for responsive user interfaces
- **Configuration & State:** Azure App Configuration with native SDK caching and jittered polling
- **Security:** Azure Active Directory for Single Sign-On and Azure RBAC for access control

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture allows incremental migration of claim types while keeping the mainframe as the system of record. Azure App Configuration and local SDK caching ensure sub-millisecond flag evaluations to protect performance SLAs without adding operational complexity for a cloud-inexperienced team.
